tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P1] Add a capped hold and a second-person proof to the Community live gate
tasks.description:
Extend the credentialed Community live gate (`packages/cli/scripts/test-community-deploy-live.ts`, `community-deploy-live-config.ts`, `community-deploy-live-proof.ts`) so an attended run can keep the new community alive for a bounded time and prove a second person.

Requirements:
- New optional arm `DORKOS_COMMUNITY_LIVE_HOLD_MINUTES`: an integer from 1 to 45. Unset means no hold. Anything else (0, 46, a decimal, text) is refused before any npm, profile or service call, with a message naming the allowed range. Read it at module scope like the other arms.
- After the existing owner proof passes: as the owner, create a one-time invite through the public HTTP contract; sign up a second local account with it; prove the member reads the owner's post, posts a reply, downloads the owner's private file with matching bytes (sha256), and that an anonymous download is still refused. This runs whether or not the hold is set.
- When the hold is set: create a fresh `0700` directory under the run's retained directory (never inside the repo), write `handoff.json` with mode `0600` holding origin, communityId, channelId, owner email and password, member email and password, and the invite link. Print only the file's path. Poll every 5 s until the hold expires or a sibling file named `done` exists. Control-C (SIGINT or SIGTERM) during the hold ends the hold at once.
- Always delete the handoff directory, then run the existing identity-checked cleanup. The hold must never be able to skip cleanup, including on timeout, interrupt, or a thrown error.
- Receipt gains `secondMemberProof: true` and `held: { minutes, endedBy: 'signal' | 'timeout' | 'interrupt' }` (absent when no hold). No credential, invite link or password enters the receipt, stdout or stderr.
- Add `DORKOS_COMMUNITY_LIVE_HOLD_MINUTES` to the paid-path table in `AGENTS.md` (the Community row's arm list) and make sure `packages/evals/src/runner/__tests__/paid-provider.test.ts` walks the new name so no turbo task can expose it. Document the arm in `specs/community-self-host-launcher/04-live-gate.md`.

Acceptance criteria and tests (each test carries a purpose comment):
- Config tests: 1 and 45 accepted; 0, 46, 1.5, "abc" refused before any process starts.
- Hold tests with a fake clock and fake cleanup: ends on `done`, on timeout, and on SIGINT; cleanup runs exactly once in each case and after a thrown error inside the hold.
- The handoff directory is `0700`, the file `0600`, and both are gone before cleanup starts.
- A test that greps the receipt and captured stdout/stderr for the fake passwords and invite token finds none.
- The second-member proof fails the gate when the member download bytes differ or the anonymous download is not refused (use the existing local HTTP fixture style).
- No live provider call is made by any test. `pnpm vitest run` on the touched test files, CLI typecheck and lint pass.
tasks.activeForm: Adding the live gate hold and second-person proof

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P1] Let the two-Desktop driver run against an existing remote Community
tasks.description:
Add a remote mode to the two-Desktop acceptance driver (`apps/e2e/community-two-desktop/`: `config.ts`, `infra.ts`, `run.ts`, `journey.ts`, the `steps-*.ts` files, `README.md`) so it can run the member journey on a community that the live gate made and is holding.

Requirements:
- New variable `DORKOS_TWO_DESKTOP_COMMUNITY_HANDOFF=<absolute path>`, read only when `DORKOS_TWO_DESKTOP_ACCEPTANCE=1`. The file is the live gate's `handoff.json` (fields: origin, communityId, channelId, owner email and password, member email and password, invite link). Refuse to start when the file is not a regular file, is not mode `0600`, sits in a directory that is not `0700`, or lacks a field. Refuse an origin that is not https.
- In remote mode, start no Postgres container and no Community server. Person A is the handoff owner; person B is the handoff member (already a member, so skip invitation steps).
- Run these steps: 5–7 and 9 (both packaged apps start in their own homes and connect through the real browser approval: signed out for A, signed in for B; both see the handoff's channel), 10–13 (switcher into the channel, post, thread reply, file byte for byte), 14–15b (nothing from the Community shows up in "this DorkOS"; reopening the channel lands where the reader left off, including a row scrolled up to), 17–18 (switcher by keyboard: Cmd+Shift+K, arrows, Enter, Escape; and phone width), 19 (neither app looks up a Community room in its local rooms), 20 and 22 (each person picks one local agent; A mentions B's agent; the scripted test reply is seen by both), 23 (B relaunches; connection, switcher order, saved spot and agent survive), 25 (Disconnect ends only this app's connection).
- Skip every other step and record each one as `skipped: remote-mode` in the receipt, so every step from 1 to 29 (with 15b) is either run or listed: 1–4 (setup and invitation, already done by the live gate), 8 and 16 (both need a second community, and remote mode starts none), 21 (needs a private channel the gate's community does not have; DOR-2186 proved it locally), and 24 and 26–29 (ownership moves, leave, expired invite, rejoin and removal change membership; DOR-2182 proved them locally). A unit test asserts the run list and the skip list together cover every step exactly once.
- Add phone-width (390 x 844) and desktop screenshots of the live origin's sign-in page and channel view.
- Cleanup removes only what the run made: both apps' connections and grants, agent enrollments, and the temporary homes. It never deletes the community or accounts (the gate does).
- The receipt records `mode: 'remote'` and the origin's host name only; no credential appears in the receipt, logs or screenshots' file names.
- Update `README.md` with a "Run against a held live community" section.

Acceptance criteria and tests:
- `__tests__/config.test.ts` gains cases: loose file mode refused, loose directory mode refused, missing field refused, http origin refused, valid handoff accepted and `infra` disabled.
- A unit test proves remote mode never calls the infra start functions (inject fakes).
- `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify` and CI still never run the driver itself. Typecheck and lint for `@dorkos/e2e` pass.
- One local dry run against a locally started Community (the driver's own infra run once, then its handoff written by hand in a private temp folder) passes the remote steps. Record the receipt path in the PR, not the file.
tasks.activeForm: Adding the two-Desktop driver remote mode

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P1] Prove the launcher and its community never need DorkOS Cloud
tasks.description:
Make "no DorkOS Cloud" a mechanical check instead of a design claim.

Requirements:
- Add a small Node preload module (for example `packages/cli/scripts/community-deploy-no-dorkos-hosts.mjs`) that, when loaded with `--import`, wraps `globalThis.fetch`, `http.request`, `https.request` and `dns.lookup` and throws a clear error for any host that is `dorkos.ai` or ends in `.dorkos.ai`. It records every refused host to a file named by an environment variable, so a test can read it.
- `pnpm --filter dorkos test:community-package` (`packages/cli/scripts/test-community-deploy-package.ts`) loads the guard into the installed launcher process through `NODE_OPTIONS` and asserts the fake-provider flow still completes and the refused-host file is empty.
- The live gate (`test-community-deploy-live.ts`) loads the same guard into the installed launcher and records `dorkosHostsContacted: []` in the receipt (the list of refused hosts; a non-empty list fails the gate after cleanup).
- The live gate reads `GET /api/v1/auth-options` on the new community and fails when it offers single sign-on (an `oidc` entry).
- A unit test in `packages/cli/src/commands/community-deploy/__tests__/fly-config-health.test.ts` asserts the rendered Fly config contains no `COMMUNITY_OIDC_` setting.

Acceptance criteria and tests:
- Mutation check, recorded in the PR: temporarily add `await fetch('https://dorkos.ai')` to the fake flow and show the package test fails, then remove it.
- Guard unit tests: `dorkos.ai`, `cloud.dorkos.ai` refused; `notdorkos.ai`, `api.github.com`, `fly.io` allowed.
- CLI typecheck, lint, and the touched tests pass. No live provider call.
tasks.activeForm: Proving the launcher never contacts DorkOS hosts

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P1] Write backup and upgrade steps for a community made with guided setup
tasks.description:
Add a section "Back up and upgrade a community made with guided setup" to `apps/community/FLY.md`, after "Pause writes for a matching backup". Today the backup, restore and upgrade commands in `apps/community/OPERATIONS.md` are written for Docker Compose, and FLY.md only says to use the providers' tools.

The section must cover, with exact commands checked against the launcher's pinned `flyctl` and `neonctl` minimum versions:
1. Find what is running: the launcher's journal path under the DorkOS data directory (`launches/community/<run-id>.json`), `fly releases --app <app> --json`, and `fly machine list --app <app> --json` for the image digest.
2. Pause writes: link to the existing section.
3. Database: `pg_dump --format=custom` over the direct TLS connection URL. Explain where the URL lives (the Fly secret `COMMUNITY_DATABASE_URL`; get it again from Neon's Connect dialog with pooling off) without printing it into shell history (read into a variable from a private file).
4. Files: copy every object from the private Tigris bucket with an S3 client (for example `aws s3 sync` with `--endpoint-url https://fly.storage.tigris.dev`) using the app's own keys, fetched from the Tigris dashboard or a new key, never by making the bucket public. Record object count and checksums.
5. Resume service: link to the existing section.
6. Rehearse a restore: follow `OPERATIONS.md` "Rehearse a restore" with its S3 variant into local Docker, and check sign-in, history, a thread and exact file bytes.
7. Upgrade: find the next release's exact image digest in its signed release manifest (the GitHub release asset the launcher reads), take and verify a backup set, deploy with `fly deploy --app <app> --image ghcr.io/dork-labs/dorkos-community@sha256:<digest> --ha=false` using a config that keeps one Machine, then run the post-upgrade checks from `OPERATIONS.md` "Upgrade and roll back".
8. Roll back: restore the matching database, files and image together; never start an older image on an upgraded database.
Also state plainly that Tigris snapshots are not turned on by guided setup, and that the launcher's completion screen does not mean backups exist.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every command is checked against the pinned CLI versions' help output (record the versions in the PR).
- Prose follows the `writing-for-humans` skill; no "mission control"/"cockpit" wording; `scripts/check-banned-words.sh` and the vocab gate pass.
- Mark the upgrade subsection "not yet rehearsed on guided setup" until task 2.1 records it; task 3.2 removes that note only if 2.1 proved a cross-version upgrade.
- Docs-only PR with `skip-changelog` and `review:light`.

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P1] Write the attended live-run checklist for DOR-2170
tasks.description:
Write `specs/community-launch-acceptance/05-live-checklist.md`: the exact procedure for the three attended paid runs (L2 journey and recovery, L3 failure and restricted credentials and interruption, L4 fresh accounts). It must hold no secret and no provider identifier.

For each run, list:
- Preconditions: the published release version (at or after the one containing #2372, #2373, #2374 and #2378, with DOR-2169's published-release gate PASS recorded); the operator's approval for the run and the budget left; tools and versions; for L3, the operator-made Fly read-only token (`fly tokens create readonly`) and Neon project-scoped API key, and a read-only note of which Fly and Neon org roles can create resources; for L4, the new accounts and a clean macOS user account.
- The exact commands and environment variables, in order. L2: live gate with `DORKOS_COMMUNITY_LIVE_HOLD_MINUTES=45`, then the two-Desktop driver with `DORKOS_TWO_DESKTOP_COMMUNITY_HANDOFF`, then the task 1.4 backup, local restore rehearsal and upgrade, then `touch <dir>/done`. L3: (a) a run with the read-only token in a private `FLY_CONFIG_DIR` (the launcher drops `FLY_API_TOKEN`), expect refusal at the first write and zero resources; (b) normal Fly login with the project-scoped key handed to `neonctl` by a method the checklist proves (the launcher drops `NEON_API_KEY`), expect the Fly app made and the Neon create refused, compare the printed recovery table with the real inventory, run `--list-incomplete`; (c) switch `neonctl` back to the normal sign-in, `--resume <run-id>`, press Control-C during `fly deploy`, `--resume` again to finish, complete owner setup and one post; (d) clean up with the printed inspect commands and compare inventories. L4: follow only `docs/self-hosting/community.mdx` from a clean account, invite a second person in another browser profile, connect a DorkOS app, add one agent, mention it.
- What to record (receipt path, ids and digests only, screenshots, timings, every unclear message) and where (`04-acceptance.md`, a DOR-2170 comment).
- Stop rules: stop and ask the operator when provider billing shows more than $2.50 spent across DOR-2170 runs, when any inventory does not match after cleanup, or when a launcher defect appears (file it as its own bug, link it as blocking DOR-2170).
- Revocation after L3 of both restricted credentials.

Acceptance: reviewed against `specs/community-launch-acceptance/02-specification.md` so every acceptance row A1 to A8 has a step that produces its evidence. Docs-only PR.

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P1] Draft the "Run your own community" guide page
tasks.description:
Draft `docs/self-hosting/community.mdx` ("Run your own community") with the `writing-for-humans` skill: plain enough for a smart 9th grader who does not code.

It covers, in order:
1. What you get: your own Community on your own Fly, Neon and Tigris accounts; your data and bills are yours; no DorkOS account is needed.
2. What you need: Fly and Neon accounts with a payment method, `flyctl` and `neonctl` signed in, `gh` signed in, a Mac (the tested platform; say plainly that Windows and Linux have not been tested).
3. Preview first: the `--dry-run` command.
4. Start: what the plan screen shows, which accounts may charge you, typing the app name to agree, the separate Tigris terms step.
5. If setup stops: the recovery table, `--list-incomplete`, `--resume <run-id>`, nothing is deleted on its own.
6. Owner setup in the browser, the one-time setup secret, why it is replaced after you sign up.
7. Invite the first person.
8. Connect DorkOS and add an agent (switcher, Add community, Connect a community, then Members and Add to community).
9. Backups and upgrades: link to the `apps/community/FLY.md` section from task 1.4.
10. Where to get help.

Rules: never "one-click"; never "mission control" or "cockpit"; a Telegram-style hookup is a connection; every claim must match evidence the spec's acceptance matrix requires. Do not add the page to `docs/self-hosting/meta.json` and do not link it from anywhere yet; that happens in task 3.2.

Open the PR with labels `skip-changelog`, `review:light` and `hold`, and do not arm it: it merges only in task 3.2 after the evidence exists. Run the banned-words and vocab gates and the site build locally.

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P2] Run the live journey and recovery check (L2)
tasks.description:
Paid, attended, operator-approved (estimate under $0.25). Follow `specs/community-launch-acceptance/05-live-checklist.md` section L2 exactly.

Preconditions: DOR-2169's published-release live gate PASS is recorded; tasks 1.1 to 1.5 are merged in the release used (or, for the gate-side tooling, run from a checkout of that release's tag plus the merged tooling commits); the operator approved this run.

Steps: run the live gate on the published release with every arm and `DORKOS_COMMUNITY_LIVE_HOLD_MINUTES=45`. During the hold: run the two-Desktop driver in remote mode against the handoff file; then follow the `FLY.md` guided-setup backup steps (pause writes, database dump, bucket copy with checksums, resume), restore into local Docker and check sign-in, history, a thread and exact file bytes; then the upgrade step (cross-version if two published releases with every launcher fix share a migration fingerprint, otherwise a same-image redeploy by the same steps, recorded as such); then `touch <dir>/done`. Let the gate clean up.

Pass criteria: gate receipt shows `ownerCreated`, `privateFileRoundTrip`, `anonymousDownloadDenied`, `secondMemberProof` true, `dorkosHostsContacted` empty, no single sign-on offered, before and after inventories identical; driver receipt outcome PASS or PASS-WITH-FINDINGS with every remote step passing, including 17 to 18 and 22; restore check passes with matching bytes; upgrade check passes. Delete the local backup copies and restore containers afterwards.

Record ids and digests only in `specs/community-launch-acceptance/04-acceptance.md` (rows A5, A6, A7, A8) and a DOR-2170 comment. Any launcher or product defect: file it as its own DOR bug, link it as blocking DOR-2170, and re-run after the fix.

Precondition: DOR-2169's published-release live gate PASS (task 4.3 of `specs/community-self-host-launcher/`) must be recorded first. Do not start this run before it.

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P2] Run the live failure, restricted-credential and interruption check (L3)
tasks.description:
Paid, attended, operator-approved (estimate under $0.15). Follow `specs/community-launch-acceptance/05-live-checklist.md` section L3.

Operator-only preconditions: the operator creates a Fly read-only token (`fly tokens create readonly`) and a Neon project-scoped API key for a throwaway project, and notes read-only which Fly and Neon org roles can create resources. Both credentials are revoked after the run.

Steps and pass criteria:
(a) With the read-only token in a private `FLY_CONFIG_DIR` (the launcher drops `FLY_API_TOKEN`; see the checklist): preflight and consent run, then the first write is refused with a clear permission message; no resource exists in either inventory.
(b) Normal Fly login, the project-scoped key handed to `neonctl` by the method the checklist proves (the launcher drops `NEON_API_KEY`): the Fly app is made and verified, the Neon project create is refused; the printed recovery table lists exactly the Fly app with its owner, possible charges, inspect command and the exact resume command; `dorkos community deploy --list-incomplete` lists the run.
(c) Switch `neonctl` back to the normal sign-in, run the printed resume command: Neon and Tigris are made; press Control-C during `fly deploy`; the launcher saves its state and prints the resume command; resume again and it finishes; complete owner setup and one post.
(d) Clean up with the printed inspect commands, checking name and org first; before and after inventories match.

Record in `04-acceptance.md` rows A2, A3, A4 (ids only, the exact messages shown) and a DOR-2170 comment. A launcher that makes a resource after a refusal, prints a wrong recovery table, or cannot resume is a defect: file it as its own DOR bug blocking DOR-2170.

Precondition: DOR-2169's published-release live gate PASS (task 4.3 of `specs/community-self-host-launcher/`) must be recorded first. Do not start this run before it.

tasks.subject: [community-launch-acceptance] [P2] Run the fresh-account walkthrough (L4, operator-only)
tasks.description:
Operator-only, paid on the new accounts (estimate under $0.25). Follow `specs/community-launch-acceptance/05-live-checklist.md` section L4.

The operator creates new Fly and Neon accounts with a payment method on an email they control, signs in to a clean macOS user account with no DorkOS data, installs the published `dorkos` release, and follows only the draft guide `docs/self-hosting/community.mdx` (task 1.6), with no other help.

Pass criteria: the dry run, consent, the first-time Tigris terms step, owner setup, inviting a second person (another browser profile), connecting a DorkOS app from the switcher and adding one local agent that answers a mention all succeed; the operator lists every unclear message or step. Cleanup by the guide's own steps leaves both new accounts with no resources.

An agent may sit with the operator to take notes and turn the unclear points into guide fixes (task 1.6's PR) or DOR bugs linked as blocking DOR-2170. Record row A1 in `04-acceptance.md` (no account names, emails or ids beyond the community id).

Precondition: DOR-2169's published-release live gate PASS (task 4.3 of `specs/community-self-host-launcher/`) must be recorded first. Do not start this run before it.
